D.why: 'Unlike' marks the contrast, and both response times appear. If you picked this, you may have marked it down for leaving out the notes on what each branch recognizes. Those notes are irrelevant to a goal about speed, so leaving them out is right.

stem: The student wants to emphasize how much less water one irrigation method required than the other. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Cotton growers in arid regions often irrigate with either furrow irrigation or drip irrigation.
• Furrow irrigation channels water along shallow trenches between crop rows.
• Drip irrigation releases water directly at plant roots through perforated tubing.
• In a 2019 field trial in Arizona, furrow-irrigated cotton used 1,100 millimeters of water per season.
• Drip-irrigated cotton in the same trial used 750 millimeters of water per season.
• The drip-irrigated plots also produced about 8 percent more cotton fiber.
choices: In the 2019 Arizona trial, drip-irrigated cotton used 350 millimeters less water per season than furrow-irrigated cotton (750 versus 1,100).
Furrow irrigation and drip irrigation, two methods common in arid regions, were both used to water cotton in a 2019 field trial in Arizona.
Because drip-irrigated cotton used 750 millimeters of water rather than 1,100, drip irrigation will cut water use by a third on any cotton farm.
In the 2019 Arizona trial, drip-irrigated plots produced about 8 percent more cotton fiber than plots watered with furrow irrigation did.
explanation: The goal limits you to one attribute, water use, and asks how big the gap is. Choice A names both methods, gives each one's water use, and states the difference outright: 350 millimeters less for drip irrigation. That puts the size of the gap at the center of the sentence, which is exactly what the goal asks for.

B.why: You picked a choice because it mentions both methods. It only lists them, though. It never says how their water use differed, so the reader learns nothing about the gap.

C.why: You noticed that this choice compares the two water amounts. But it then claims the same savings will happen 'on any cotton farm.' The notes describe one trial in Arizona, so they don't support that claim.

D.why: This choice does contrast the two methods, but on fiber yield, not water use. The goal asked how much less water one method needed, so the comparison is on the wrong attribute.
